extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (patent owners/representatives) handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and prosecuting patents in ex parte reexamination proceedings, including claim construction, statutory compliance (35 U.S.C. 112, 132, 119, 305), use of prior art, amendments to claims/specification, and Office procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: During reexamination, claims are given the broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification; limitations in the specification are not read into the claims (In re Yamamoto). For reexamination involving claims of an expired patent, claim construction pursuant to Phillips v. AWH Corp. (ordinary and customary meaning) should be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply broadest reasonable interpretation during reexamination unless claims are expired (then use Phillips). Consider written statements of the patent owner of record (37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) and 1.552) after reexamination is ordered to determine proper claim meaning when applying patents/printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory presumption of validity not applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory presumption of validity, 35 U.S.C. 282, has no application in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply the 'presumption of validity' standard in reexamination (see In re Etter). Evaluate patentability based on reexamination standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 35 U.S.C. 112 examination limited to amendatory matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new claims are presented or any part of the disclosure is amended, examination under 35 U.S.C. 112 should be limited to the amendatory (new language) matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A limitation present in the original patent claim that is repeated in a newly presented or amended claim generally cannot be examined under 35 U.S.C. 112 unless the amendatory matter creates the issue. Rewriting a dependent claim as independent cannot be examined under §112 unless rewriting raises a new question (e.g., lack of antecedent). See MPEP §2163 - §2173.05(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112 issues to consider for new/amended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance of new or amended claims with the enablement and/or written description requirements of the first paragraph, and compliance with the second paragraph of 35 U.S.C.112, should be considered as to the amendatory and new text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should apply MPEP §2163 - §2173.05(v) for detailed guidance; focus only on the new/amendatory text for enablement/written description/definiteness issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new matter (35 U.S.C. 132/305)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 305 provides for examination under 35 U.S.C. 132, which prohibits the introduction of new matter into the disclosure. New matter added to claims or affecting claim limitations should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, for failing to meet the written description requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for new matter whenever claims or specification are amended in reexamination; rely on MPEP §2163.06 regarding relationship between written description and the new matter prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to the specification must comply with 35 U.S.C. 112
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to the specification in a reexamination proceeding can redefine the scope of terms in a claim so that the claim is no longer clear or is not supported by the specification, causing failure to comply with 35 U.S.C. 112 even if claims are not amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should ensure specification amendments do not create written-description or enablement problems; a specification amendment may also enlarge claim scope (see related rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must not enlarge scope of original patent claims (35 U.S.C. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new or amended claims are presented or any part of the disclosure is amended, the claims of the reexamination proceeding should be examined under 35 U.S.C. 305 to determine whether they enlarge the scope of the original claims. 'No proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of a claim of the patent will be permitted in a reexamination proceeding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject any claim that enlarges scope under 35 U.S.C. 305; employ form paragraph 22.11 when making such a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for determining enlargement of scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim presented in reexamination 'enlarges the scope' of the patent where the claim is broader than each and every claim of the patent. A claim is broadened if it contains any conceivable product or process which would not have infringed the original patent; being broader in any one respect is enough even if narrower in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §1412.03 for guidance on what is broadening; identify and explain the claim limitations that broaden the scope in the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection procedure for enlarged claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claim in a reexamination proceeding which enlarges the scope of the claims of the patent should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.11 (Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 305, Claim Enlarges Scope of Patent - Ex Parte Reexamination). In bracket 2 identify and explain the claim limitations considered to broaden the scope. Follow Examiner Note guidance in MPEP §2258.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling patents subject to prior Office or Court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some patent claims have been the subject of a prior Office or court decision, those claims not subject to reexamination because of prior adjudication should be identified; see MPEP §2242. If other proceedings are copending, see MPEP §2282-§2286.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior Office/court decisions raise grounds not based on patents/printed publications, the examiner's Office action should clearly state that claims have not been examined as to those non-patent/printed publication grounds (37 CFR 1.552(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on 'live' claims in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office's determination in both the order and the examination stage is generally limited solely to review of the 'live' claims (existing claims not held invalid by a final decision) for which reexamination has been requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requester must set forth pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested (35 U.S.C. 302 and 37 CFR 1.510(b)). Failure to apply the art to certain claims generally precludes reexamination of those claims. The Office may nonetheless exercise discretion to reexamine non-requested claims or add claims if new art raises an SNQ (35 U.S.C. 303(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirements not proper in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction requirements cannot be made in a reexamination proceeding since no statutory basis exists for restriction in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding claims to a 'separate and distinct' invention would be considered an enlargement of scope (see Ex parte Wikdahl and MPEP §1412.03). Do not issue restriction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary matters permitted in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters ancillary to reexamination which are necessary and incident to patentability will be considered (e.g., amendments to the specification to correct inadvertent failures to claim foreign priority or continuing status if necessary to overcome a reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reexamination to make corrections that are incident to patentability, but observe other statutory limits (e.g., new matter prohibition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming foreign and domestic priority in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may obtain foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) by submission of the certified copy in reexamination; may also submit both the priority claim and certified copy for the first time in some circumstances. However, addition or correction of benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) after issuance is prohibited for patents matured from applications filed on or after Nov 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submission is late for patents matured from apps filed on/after Nov 29, 2000, the patent owner must file a grantable petition for an unintentionally delayed priority claim under 37 CFR 1.55(c) or 1.78(a)(3) as appropriate. No renewal of previously made priority/benefit claims is necessary during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship may be made during reexamination via petition under 37 CFR 1.324 and MPEP §1481.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 1.324 petition is granted, a Certificate of Correction will not be separately issued because the change will be merged into the reexamination certificate; ensure required procedures and information are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits/declarations in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131(a) and 1.132 may be utilized in a reexamination proceeding; however, a 1.131(a) affidavit may not be used to 'swear behind' a reference patent if the reference patent claims the 'same invention'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference patent claims the same invention, consider use of 37 CFR 1.131(c) or, if appropriate, raising the issue in an interference or via a reissue application (see MPEP §718 and §1449.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues not considered in reexamination (scope limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions other than those indicated (e.g., public use/on sale, conduct issues, abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) for first-to-invent regime, etc.) raised by parties should be noted but are not within the scope of reexamination and thus will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.03 (Issue Not Within Scope of Ex Parte Reexamination) to inform the patentee; advise that filing a reissue application may be desirable if the patentee wishes those issues to be considered. If such issues were independently discovered by the examiner but not raised by parties, the examiner will not note them in an Office action because 37 CFR 1.552(c) only addresses issues 'raised by the patent owner or the third party requester.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests filed on patents after reissue are denied
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for reexamination is filed on a patent after it has been reissued, reexamination will be denied because the patent on which the request is based has been surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reexamine a reissued patent, a new request based on the specification and claims of the reissue patent must be filed. If a reissue issues after a reexamination request was filed, treat the reissue patent text as the patent text for any amendments filed subsequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: No preissuance submissions in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Because reexamination is a post-issuance proceeding, a preissuance submission under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) (third-party preissuance submissions) is not permitted to be filed in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any preissuance submission inadvertently filed in a reexamination proceeding is not to be entered and will be expunged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of previously cited/considered art ('old art')
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a rejection, the examiner should check the patent's file history to ascertain whether the art to be relied upon was previously cited/considered in an earlier concluded examination of the patent ('old art').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejection is based on a combination of old art and newly cited art, it is proper (In re Hiniker). If old art is the sole basis, treatment depends on whether reexamination was ordered on/after Nov 2, 2002 (see related rubrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying old art as sole basis for SNQ for reexaminations ordered on/after Nov 2, 2002
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered on or after November 2, 2002, reliance solely on old art does not necessarily preclude the existence of a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) based exclusively on that old art; determinations are fact-specific on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A SNQ may arise where old art is presented/viewed in a new light or in a different way in view of a material new argument or interpretation. Where an Office action newly determines an SNQ based solely on old art, include form paragraph 22.01.01 and explain how the old art supports the SNQ (insert the old art and explanation in the brackets per Examiner Note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Portola Packaging for reexaminations ordered prior to Nov 2, 2002
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered prior to November 2, 2002, old art generally cannot be used as the sole basis for a rejection; In re Portola Packaging controls, subject to specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior art was previously relied upon to reject a claim in a concluded prior related Office proceeding, the Office will not conduct reexamination based only on that prior art. Prior related Office proceedings include the application that matured into the patent, reissue applications, and prior reexaminations. Mere citation without discussion of relevance does not preclude reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for determining termination under Portola Packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing ongoing reexaminations ordered prior to Nov 2, 2002, Office personnel must follow procedures to decide whether prosecution must be terminated to comply with Portola Packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures include: (a) confirm order date; (b) determine prior related proceedings and which prior art was relied upon or cited and discussed; (c) base rejections on art not previously relied upon/discussed; (d) withdraw rejections based only on previously relied-upon/discussed art; (e) terminate prosecution if remaining rejections are solely based on such prior art; Director may search for new art (see MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unusual fact patterns concerning previously considered art
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual fact patterns (e.g., partial discussion of a textbook, mistaken assessment that a reference was not prior art, incomplete foreign-language translation, cumulative/repetitive references) require case-specific consideration and may be referred to CRU or TC Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: if only part of a textbook was discussed, indicate which portion was considered; if prior translation was incomplete, a more complete translation may justify reexamination; cumulative references that substantially reiterate verbatim teachings of earlier references are generally not considered but are expected to be rare. Bring unusual cases to higher authority for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices and wording when terminating or withdrawing based on Portola
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is terminated under Portola Packaging, the Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate should state the termination and that no patentability determination has been made. If a rejection is withdrawn under Portola, the Office action should state the withdrawal and that no patentability determination has been made in view of that prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific wording provided in MPEP for Notices and withdrawn Office actions to ensure clarity about lack of patentability determinations when terminating or withdrawing under Portola.

rubrics_metrics.name: Res judicata and collateral estoppel in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims finally held valid by a Federal Court after all appeals will be withdrawn from consideration and not reexamined in reexamination; res judicata is not appropriate. Collateral estoppel may be applied in reexamination where an issue decided in court applies to the claims being reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §2242 and §2286 for Office policy when a Federal Court decision exists on the merits; identify claims not subject to reexamination because of prior adjudication and apply collateral estoppel carefully when applicable.
